cuts.raw_narration: The newly hatched Chimera Ant King, a small greenish humanoid with a long segmented tail, stands calmly in the cavern surrounded by his own species. A turtle-shelled ant named Peggy nervously warns him that the queen's organs have been severely damaged. In a single instant blood splatters onto a purple book on the floor, and when the shot pulls back Peggy lies decapitated, blood pooling around his severed head. The King stands over the body indifferently, chin lifted, cold and unimpressed.

Colt begs Pitou to heal the dying queen. Pitou, her clawed hands resting heavily on his shoulders, gives a chillingly cheerful smile and refuses, saying that now that the King has been born the queen simply doesn't matter anymore. She turns and walks off down a dark tunnel with the other guards, leaving Colt frozen and speechless as she wags one finger in cruel, playful dismissal.

Told the feast is on the roof, the King decides it will be faster to go from the outside. He smashes straight through the solid rock wall of the nest in a huge explosion of dust and debris. When the smoke clears, a fresh circular opening has been punched through the mountain and the King steps out onto the ledge above a vast green valley, seeing the sky for the first time.

Above a canyon river, the winged ant Colt lands in front of the hunters Morel and Knov holding a white flag on a staff. Sweating and shaking, he announces that the ants surrender unconditionally — but only on one condition: the hunters must save the queen's life, because she can no longer give birth. Then he drops the bombshell that the King has already been born, far ahead of schedule.

In a cultivated field Pitou kneels before the King and cheerfully begins explaining that rare humans can be identified by focusing the eyes to see the aura around a body. Mid-sentence the King's tail whips out and cracks her across the face, knocking her sideways. He turns with a wide-eyed, almost surprised expression — he had genuinely intended to kill her. Pitou kneels back up unfazed, a trickle of blood on her cheek, closes her eyes and bows her head in submission. The King curls a thin sinister smirk and tells her she has earned his respect.

In the cavern, the Chimera Ant squad leaders stand around Peggy's cracked, empty shell in silent shock, realizing the King sees them as nothing more than food. The lion-like leader Leol steps forward with a scheming, sharp-toothed grin and proposes the unthinkable: since the queen can no longer reproduce, why shouldn't each of them try to become a king themselves and build their own kingdoms? The other squad leaders listen with growing, dangerous interest as the colony quietly begins to fracture.
